This appeal is preferred by accused No.1 against the judgment of conviction and sentence passed against him by the Court of II Additional District and Sessions Judge and Special Judge at Dharwad in Special S.C.No.13/2017.

Further, accused No.2 was found guilty of the offences punishable under Sections 504, 506 and 324 of IPC.

3. Insofar as accused No.2 is concerned, he was released on probation of good conduct subject to execution of self bond along with a surety for an amount of Rs.25,000/- with a direction to appear and receive the sentence when called upon during the period of one year.

4. The State has not preferred any appeal in respect of acquittal of accused Nos. 3 and 4 and also not questioned the release of accused No.2 on probation of good conduct, under Sections 3 and 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act.

sentences.text: 5. The complainant preferred Crl.A.100321/2019, insofar as acquittal of accused Nos.1 to 4 of the charges NC: 2024:KHC-D:7686-DB leveled against them.

The material on record reveal that when the said appeal was listed before the Court on 23.06.2023, the appellant's counsel filed a memo praying to withdraw the appeal as the complainant was not interested to proceed with the matter.
Hence the said appeal was dismissed as withdrawn.
6. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned Addl. SPP and perused the evidence and material on record.
7. The charges were framed against accused Nos. 1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Sections 342, 376, 504, 324 and 506 read with Section 34 of the IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act.
It is the case of the prosecution that, on 11.02.2017, at about 1.45 pm, accused No.1 asked the victim/complainant to give soap to wash his hands and dragged her inside his house.

He wrongfully confined her in the house by locking the door and committed forcible sexual intercourse and also threatened her with dire consequences in case she NC: 2024:KHC-D:7686-DB disclosed the said fact to others.

Further, on 13.02.2017, at about 7.00 pm, when the victim's mother PW2 questioned accused No.2 about his act, the accused abused her in filthy words and accused No.2 voluntarily caused hurt to the complainant with a club.
Further, on 16.02.2017, at about 8.00 pm, the accused persons went to the house of the complainant and threatened her mother with dire consequences.

8. Learned Sessions Judge having appreciated the oral and documentary evidence adduced on record came to the conclusion that, even though, the prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused No.1 for the offence under Section 376 of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act, but nevertheless, the evidence on record and prosecution materials clearly bring the case within the ambit of Section 7 of the POCSO Act which deals with the evidence of sexual assault which prescribes a lesser punishment under Section 8 of the said Act.

The learned Sessions Judge has observed that on the date of incident, first accused called the victim girl and dragged her inside the house and thereby committed sexual assault on her by touching her body with sexual intention which clearly indicates that though he has not actually committed sexual intercourse but, nevertheless he has sexually assaulted her by touching her body with sexual intent.

Therefore, even though, the gravity of offence under Section 4 of the POCSO Act is not proved in the present case, certainly accused is to be held guilty of committing sexual assault as contemplated under Section 7 of the Act, which is punishable under Section 8 of the said Act.

10. Further, learned Sessions Judge appreciating the evidence of PW.1, held that her statement is consistent with the complaint allegations insofar as accused No.1 dragging and confining her in his house and bolting the door from outside as it is not specifically denied by the defence, hence, held that the prosecution has NC: 2024:KHC-D:7686-DB proved the offence under Section 342 of IPC as against accused No.1.

The learned Sessions Judge has further observed that the defence side has nowhere controverted the allegations that the second accused has assaulted PW1 with M.O.No.1 and not denied the said accused having abused etc.

Therefore, it is held that guilt of the second accused so far offence under Sections 504, 506 and 324 of IPC stands proved, even though those allegations were not proved against accused Nos.3 and 4.
12.
Ex.P1 is the complaint lodged by the victim (PW.1).
On perusal of the same, goes to show that alleged incident took place on 11.02.2017 at about 1 p.m.

It is averred in the complaint that, when the complainant/victim was sitting in front of her house, accused No.1 called her to give soap to wash his hands and when she went near him he dragged her by hand held her mouth and took her inside his house and locked the door and went away.

Thereafter, returned after 10-15 NC:
2024:KHC-D:7686-DB minutes and committed rape on her and threatened her with dire consequences saying that if she disclosed the incident to anyone, she will be killed.
13. The complaint is lodged on 17.02.2017.
In Ex.P.1, it is stated that since, the complainant's mother was suffering from illness, complainant did not disclose the matter to her and after 2-3 days she informed about the incident.
Her mother called the accused and enquired with him, but he abused and assaulted etc.
Thereafter, on 16.02.2017 at about 8 p.m. accused Nos.1 to 4 came to complainant's house and threatened them etc.
14. The complainant/victim is examined as PW.1.
In her chief examination, she has corroborated the complaint version.
However, in the cross examination, she has totally denied the prosecution case.
She has stated that the accused has not committed rape on her and not even touched her body and not committed sexual assault on her.
She has stated that as per the say of her mother and Police, she has given statement before the Magistrate.
She NC: 2024:KHC-D:7686-DB admitted that there is a civil dispute between the two families and because of the civil dispute and as per the say of her mother she lodged the complaint.
15. PWs.2 and 3 are the parents of PW.1/victim.
In chief examination, PW.2 has deposed about the victim informing the incident to her.
It is relevant to note that as per Ex.P1, PW1 informed the matter to her mother after 2- 3 days, whereas PW2 in her evidence has stated that the matter was informed to her on the very next day.
If the evidence of PW.2 is appreciated, it can be seen that the victim informed PW.2 that accused No.1 asked her to bring the soap and then spoiled her.
She has not deposed that the accused has dragged the victim by her hand and took her inside the house and locked the door and then returned and committed sexual assault on her.

In the cross examination,
she has admitted about the civil dispute between the family of accused No.1 and her family since many years and in this connection her husband had - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7686-DB demanded a share in the property and there was quarrel etc.

16. The evidence of PW.2 is not in consonance with the prosecution case that the appellant/accused No.1 dragged the victim by holding her hand and took inside the house and bolted the door and Arunagouda S/O Bapanagouda Patil @ ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143614873/
4 committed sexual intercourse etc.

sentences.text: She is a hearsay witness.

PW.1 herself having denied the case of prosecution in the cross examination and having admitted that she lodged the complaint and gave statement before the Court as per the say of her mother and Police, the evidence of PW.2 does not inspire the confidence of the Court.
17. PW.3 is victim's father.
However, he is also a hearsay witness.
He has stated that on the date of incident he was in Hubballi.
He has been treated hostile by the prosecution.
He has admitted that the incident was informed to him by his wife i.e. PW.2.
He has not deposed anywhere that incident was informed to him by his daughter i.e. victim.
PWs.4 to 7, 9, 14 and 15 have not supported the case of prosecution.
Their evidence is not helpful to the prosecution case.

19. The learned Addl. SPP has contended that PW.6 is an independent witness and he speaks about the incident as well as panchayath conducted and therefore, the same establish that there was an incident which took place on 11.02.2017.

It is his contention that the trial Court after appreciating the entire evidence including the medical evidence has convicted the accused for lesser offence,
which is in accordance with law.
20. A perusal of the evidence of PW.6, who has been treated hostile by the prosecution case goes to show that he was informed by victim's mother about the incident.
He has stated that they called the accused and conducted a panchayath.
He has only stated that, he came to know about accused committing rape on the victim and stated that, accused persons agreed to perform the marriage of accused No.1 with the victim.

He has admitted - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7686-DB in the cross-examination that on 16.02.2017, at about 8 p.m., CW.6 i.e.
PW.2 having called him, CWs.9 and 11 to their house and informed the incident which took place on 11.02.2017.
However, he has denied having stated before the Police as per Ex.P9, his previous statement recorded during investigation.
21. Nextly, the prosecution has relied on the medical evidence to prove the sexual assault committed on the victim and injury sustained by her in the incident.
22. Prosecution has examined PWs.11 and 13- medical officers.
PW.11 has examined both accused No.1 as well as the victim.
The report with regard to the examination of accused No.1 is marked as Ex.P15.
He has stated that he has collected the clothes of the victim and sent to FSL examination and after receipt of the FSL report, he has given his final opinion as per EX.P15.
FSL report issued by PW.12 which is marked as Ex.P17 is however not helpful to the prosecution.

sentences.text: PW.11 has deposed that he examined the victim girl on 17.02.2017 and noticed on injury (contusion) measuring about 2X2 Cms on her right knee.
The said injury stated to be simple in nature.

The wound certificate is marked as Ex.P16.
24.
According to the prosecution and as per Ex.P1, on the next day of the incident which took place on 11.02.2017, accused No.2 abused the victim and assaulted her with the club.
Even in the wound certificate / Ex.P16, the history mentioned with regard to the said injury is that, due to assault on 12.02.2017.
Hence, the said injury is not on account of the incident which is alleged to have taken place on 11.02.2017.
25. PW.13 has issued Ex.P.19 after the examination of PW1.
He has deposed that on 17.02.2017, he examined the victim girl who came with a history of sexual assault on her by accused No.1 on 11.02.2017.
The history alleged to have been furnished by the victim is not in consonance with the case of prosecution and as per the - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7686-DB complaint averments.

In the history furnished, it is stated that the accused after confining the victim girl in his house by locking the door, returned to the house after one hour and bit her breast and touched her private part etc.
The same is not at all whispered by PW.1 in her chief examination.
PW.13 has not noticed any bite marks.
He has opined that after performing the physical and genital examination, there is no evidence of forcible sexual intercourse nor it confirms the sexual intercourse or assault.
26. It is relevant to see that in Ex.P.16 issued by PW.11 with regard to the examination conducted on PW.1 at 5 a.m. on 17.02.2017, injury said to have been caused on 12.02.2017 due to assault.
It was not disclosed to PW.11 with regard to any sexual assault said to have taken place on 11.02.2017.
PW.11 has issued the wound certificate marked as Ex.P.16 regarding the injury sustained to the right knee of PW.1 measuring 2 cm x 2cm.
PW.13 has examined PW.1 at 8 p.m. subsequent to - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7686-DB her examination conducted by PW.11, wherein, history furnished is that she was sexually assaulted.
Hence, there is material discrepancy in the prosecution case.

27. In the light of the admission made by PW.1 that she gave complaint and statement before the Court as per the say of her mother and police, serious doubt arises about the genuineness of the prosecution case.

Having re-appreciated the entire evidence and material on record, we find that the evidence and material on record is not sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts for the charged offences to confirm the conviction and sentence passed against the appellant/accused No.1.
The victim has denied the prosecution case in her cross examination.
PW.1 as well as PW.2 have admitted the civil dispute between both the families, existing since many years.
It is stated that in this regard there was quarrel etc.
The parties are closely related to each other.
Accused No.1 is the cousin of the victim girl.
The complaint was lodged after six days.

In - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7686-DB the complaint itself it is stated that on 16.02.2017, at about 8.00 p.m.,
there was a quarrel wherein accused Nos.1 to 4 came to the house of the complainant, abused etc.
It appears the said incident prompted the complainant to lodge a complaint.

29. In view of the above discussion and for the forgoing reasons, we find that the conviction and sentence passed against accused No.1 is not in accordance with law and the same is liable to be set aside.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed.

(ii) The judgment and order dated 28.06.2018 convicting the appellant/accused No.1 for the offences punishable under Section 342 of IPC and Section 7 read with Section 8 of POCSO Act is hereby set aside.
(iii) Appellant/accused No.1 is acquitted of the above charges.
(iv) His Bail bond stands cancelled.
(v) Fine amount, if any deposited, the same shall be refunded to the appellant/accused No.1.
